question: Where does fertilisation usually occur in the female reproductive system?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Oviduct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Fertilisation** in humans typically occurs in the **oviduct (also known as the fallopian tube)**, which is a part of the female reproductive system.
 
• The **oviduct** is a narrow, muscular tube that connects the ovaries to the uterus and serves as the site where the male sperm meets the female egg (ovum).
 
• When an egg is released from the ovary during ovulation, it is captured by the **fimbriae** (finger-like projections) at the end of the oviduct and transported into the tube where fertilisation takes place.
 
• The fertilised egg (zygote) begins cell division as it travels through the oviduct a
